name: ABF substrates
thesis: AI accelerators need far larger, higher-layer-count substrates than any prior chip, and a five-firm oligopoly is heading back into shortage on what suppliers call a three-year super-cycle.

gauge.rationale: Supply-demand is tipping back into imbalance in H1 2026 and widening through 2028. Substrate area per chip is exploding (Rubin +75% over Blackwell), the top five hold ~74%, and upstream glass-fiber/copper-foil constraints are extending lead times — but it is re-tightening rather than acutely sold out today.

metrics.label: Top-5 market concentration (Unimicron, Ibiden, AT&S, Nan Ya, Shinko)
Rubin GPU substrate area vs Blackwell
AI-server PCB/substrate volume vs traditional server

why_it_gates: The ABF substrate is the rigid board the packaged die sits on; without enough high-layer-count substrate — and the glass-fiber cloth, copper foil and copper-clad laminate feeding it — a finished accelerator cannot be assembled even when wafers, HBM and packaging exist. Qualifying a new substrate supplier takes years, so capacity cannot flex quickly to meet AI demand.

catalysts.text: Substrate price increases and lead-time extensions confirm the imbalance returning in H1 2026.
Three-year ABF super-cycle as AI GPU, CPU and ASIC substrate area keeps scaling.
Upstream T-Glass / copper-foil / CCL relief (or further tightening) sets the pace of substrate output.

what_loosens_it: Aggressive Taiwanese capacity expansions coming online, resolution of the glass-fiber (T-Glass) and copper-foil upstream constraints, or any slowdown in AI-server build rates.

developments.text: AI chip demand tightening ABF supply; suppliers see a three-year upcycle starting H1 2026 and widening into 2027–2028.
Unimicron reports Jan 2026 revenue NT$10.2B (+34.5% YoY); maintains record 2026 capex of NT$25B+ for high-end ABF.
